papers.title: Rational High-Throughput Screening of Cocrystals: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework Based on Morgan Fingerprints and Cross-Attention.
papers.abstract: Aiming to address the problems of high blindness in traditional screening methods, insufficient granularity of feature representation, and poor interpretability of existing machine learning prediction models in the field of cocrystal research and development, we propose a cocrystal prediction method based on Morgan fingerprints and the cross-attention mechanism. First, a high-quality cocrystal data set is constructed, and Morgan fingerprints are employed to characterize molecular structures. Subsequently, a fingerprint-driven cross-attention model is developed to capture the feature interactio
papers.summary: The authors developed an explainable deep learning framework that predicts cocrystal formation by combining Morgan fingerprints with a cross-attention mechanism. This approach aims to reduce the trial-and-error nature of traditional cocrystal screening and improve model interpretability. The method is validated on a curated high-quality cocrystal dataset.

papers.title: Deep learning of tautomer stability from crystallographic proton positions.
papers.abstract: Tautomerism plays a central role in molecular recognition, physicochemical properties, and chemical reactivity, yet rapid identification of stable tautomeric states remains a persistent challenge in molecular design and structure-based drug discovery. Quantum-mechanical approaches are often too computationally demanding for library-scale application, while rule-based and 3D-dependent machine-learning methods remain limited in either transferability or throughput. Here, we show that experimentally resolved hydrogen positions in the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD) provide a powerful large-sc
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that experimentally determined hydrogen positions in the Cambridge Structural Database can be used to train a deep learning model for predicting stable tautomeric states. This approach offers a fast, transferable alternative to quantum-mechanical calculations and rule-based methods, enabling library-scale tautomer identification for drug discovery and molecular design.

papers.title: xLSTM-based deep learning model for predicting anticancer Activity of pyrano[3,2-a]phenazine hybrid derivatives: Proof of concept.
papers.abstract: Finding novel treatments is a long and complex process involving extensive drug discovery, experimental testing, and preclinical research. Computational quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling can support this process by enabling rapid prediction of biological activity and identification of molecular features associated with activity. This study presents a proof-of-concept deep-learning-based QSAR framework for predicting the biological activity of pyrano[3,2-a]phenazine hybrid derivatives. The proposed framework combines an Extended Long Short-Term Memory (xLSTM) architec
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study applies an Extended Long Short-Term Memory (xLSTM) deep learning architecture to QSAR modeling, predicting anticancer activity of pyrano[3,2-a]phenazine hybrid derivatives. The work demonstrates that a modern sequence-modeling architecture can be adapted to molecular activity prediction, offering a computational alternative to traditional QSAR approaches. As a proof of concept, it establishes feasibility but requires broader validation across larger and more diverse chemical datasets.

papers.title: S100A8/A9-TMEM24 axis drives podocyte injury by impairing autophagy: A novel theranostic target for early diabetic nephropathy.
papers.abstract: To establish a comprehensive theranostic framework for early-stage diabetic kidney disease (DKD) by validating serum S100A8/A9 as a highly sensitive diagnostic biomarker and exploring therapeutic strategies targeting the S100A9/transmembrane protein 24 (TMEM24) signaling axis to restore podocyte autophagy.
papers.summary: This study identifies serum S100A8/A9 as a sensitive biomarker for early diabetic kidney disease and shows that the S100A9-TMEM24 signaling axis drives podocyte injury by impairing autophagy. Targeting this axis may offer a new therapeutic strategy to restore podocyte health in early DKD.

papers.title: AIDrugDesigner: a web server for drug-like molecules generation and optimization.
papers.abstract: Designing molecules with predefined properties remains a critical yet challenging task in drug discovery. Recent advances in deep learning have demonstrated strong potential in accelerating the identification of novel compounds with desired properties and activities. However, the implementation and running of these models often present difficulties due to varying environments and the requisite for additional coding competencies.
papers.summary: AIDrugDesigner is a web server that makes deep-learning-based drug-like molecule generation and optimization accessible without coding or environment setup. It packages existing generative models into a user-friendly interface for designing compounds with predefined properties, lowering the barrier for medicinal chemists and non-programmers.

papers.title: FuTCM-PDD: a multi-level information fusion framework integrating KAN modeling and AutoML for phenotype-based drug discovery from Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.abstract: Phenotype-based drug discovery has attracted increasing attention due to its critical role in first-in-class drug development and higher clinical translation rates. Chinese Materia Medica (CMM), with its emphasis on properties and efficacies, provides a unique framework for phenotype-oriented therapeutic discovery. We developed an AI-driven framework, FuTCM-PDD, that integrates CMMs, compounds, targets, pathways, pharmacological effects, CMM efficacies, and CMM properties to enable phenotype-based drug discovery. For drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction, a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) m
papers.summary: FuTCM-PDD is an AI framework that fuses multi-level information—Traditional Chinese Medicine compounds, targets, pathways, pharmacological effects, and CMM properties/efficacies—to support phenotype-based drug discovery. It uses a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) for drug-target interaction prediction combined with AutoML, aiming to bridge TCM knowledge with modern therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: Cryptotanshinone and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I from Salvia miltiorrhiza: integrated in vitro and computational evaluation of their antidiabetic potential.
papers.abstract: Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (Lamiaceae) is a traditional medicinal plant rich in bioactive tanshinones with diverse pharmacological properties. However, comparative information regarding experimentally measured activity and computational interaction profiles of individual tanshinones remains limited. This study aimed to compare cryptotanshinone (1) and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I (2), isolated from S. miltiorrhiza, using an integrated in vitro and computational approach. The compounds were obtained through activity-informed phytochemical fractionation and evaluated for inhibition of α-glucosidase
papers.summary: This study isolated two tanshinone compounds from Salvia miltiorrhiza and compared their antidiabetic potential using both laboratory enzyme inhibition assays and computational docking. Both cryptotanshinone and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I showed inhibitory activity against α-glucosidase, with computational analysis supporting their binding interactions. The work provides comparative evidence for these natural products as potential antidiabetic agents.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Immune Dysregulation and Candidate Drug Targets in Endometriosis.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disorder affecting 5-10% of women of reproductive age and is associated with chronic pain and infertility. While research has mainly focused on local lesions, systemic immune dysfunction is increasingly implicated in disease pathogenesis. This study employs single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from women with endometriosis and unaffected controls, combined with integrative analysis of publicly available datasets of menstrual blood and endometrial tissues, to uncover immune dysregulation and therapeutic targ
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from women with endometriosis and controls, integrated with public datasets from menstrual blood and endometrial tissue, to characterize systemic immune dysregulation. The analysis identifies altered immune cell states and candidate drug targets, suggesting that endometriosis involves broader systemic immune changes beyond local lesions.

papers.title: Physical priors improve performance of structure-based binding affinity models.
papers.abstract: Structure-based drug discovery is a widely used paradigm for the rational design of novel small molecule therapeutics. However, the benefits conferred by the use of structural information has seen limited adoption in machine learning, where ligand-only ("2D") models are still the industry standard for molecular property or binding affinity prediction. Structure-based ("3D") ML models for binding-affinity prediction promise to present a clear advantage, but have not yet overtaken existing 2D models. Here, we show that physics-based priors can improve predictive performance of structure-based mo
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint demonstrates that incorporating physics-based priors into structure-based machine learning models improves their ability to predict small molecule binding affinities. The authors show that these physically informed 3D models can outperform traditional ligand-only 2D approaches, addressing a key limitation in computational drug discovery.

papers.title: From Glycan Biology to Drug Candidates: An Integrated Sialylation Niche Index and AI-Guided Therapeutic Framework for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) responds poorly (<20%) to immune checkpoint blockade. Since sialylation suppresses anti-tumour immunity through Siglec signalling independently of the PD-L1/PD-1 axis, we mapped its prognostic landscape in HNSCC by integrating prognostic modelling, molecular subtyping, and AI-guided drug discovery. Methods: Transcriptomic data from seven GEO cohorts and TCGA-HNSC (n = 501) were analysed with a 1204-gene sialylation compendium. The Sialylation Niche Index (SNI) was built in TCGA-HNSC from 117 machine-learning algorithm combinations (nomi
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data from multiple HNSCC cohorts to build a Sialylation Niche Index (SNI), a prognostic model based on sialylation-related genes, and uses AI-guided approaches to identify potential drug candidates targeting this pathway. The work highlights sialylation as an immune-evasion mechanism independent of PD-1/PD-L1 and proposes it as a therapeutic target for immunotherapy-resistant head and neck cancers.

papers.title: Biosynthetic Diversity of Marine-Derived Streptomyces Natural Products: Integrating Genome Mining, Multi-Omics, and Translational Drug Discovery Strategies.
papers.abstract: Marine-derived Streptomyces are among the most prolific producers of structurally diverse and biologically active natural products. Adaptation to unique marine environments, including deep-sea sediments, hydrothermal vents, mangrove ecosystems, marine invertebrates, and hypersaline habitats, has promoted the evolution of specialized biosynthetic systems capable of generating a broad spectrum of secondary metabolites. These metabolites include polyketides, non-ribosomal peptides (NRPs), ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs), terpenoids, alkaloids, and hybrid
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how marine-derived Streptomyces bacteria produce diverse bioactive natural products, shaped by their adaptation to extreme marine habitats. It highlights the integration of genome mining, multi-omics approaches, and translational drug discovery strategies to uncover and develop these compounds. The work positions marine Streptomyces as a rich but underexplored source for new therapeutics.

papers.title: Benzamides of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles as Anticancer Scaffolds: Synthesis, In Silico and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Indoles and benzimidazoles are important nitrogen-containing heterocyclic scaffolds and are a cornerstone of synthetic drugs. In this study, benzamides of 2-aminophenylindoles and 2-aminophenylbenzimidazoles were synthesized and evaluated for their potential. Further, they were also subjected to computational studies for their ADMET profiling and binding with target proteins. Methods: The synthesized compounds were characterized by ATR-FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR and electrospray ionization mass spectroscopy (ESI-MS). They were screened for their in vitro antibacterial activit
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of benzamide derivatives of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles and evaluated them for anticancer potential. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically, tested in vitro for antibacterial activity, and subjected to in silico ADMET profiling and molecular docking against target proteins. The work identifies these scaffolds as promising starting points for further anticancer drug development.

papers.title: Cracking ERα Y537S Resistance: Explainable Machine Learning-Guided Discovery and Molecular Dynamics Validation of Stable Candidate Ligands.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endocrine resistance due to activating mutations in the estrogen receptor alpha (ERα), especially Y537S, is still a big challenge in the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and there is a need to develop new small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome ligand-independent receptor activation. We used an integrated machine learning and molecular dynamics (MD)-based virtual screening (VS) approach to identify potential computationally prioritized hits of ERα Y537S in this study. Methods: The dataset (~3353 compounds) was characterized using molecular finger
papers.summary: This study combines explainable machine learning with molecular dynamics simulations to discover small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome the Y537S mutation in estrogen receptor alpha, a key driver of endocrine resistance in breast cancer. The authors screened ~3353 compounds and prioritized candidate ligands that remain stably bound to the mutant receptor, offering a computational pipeline for tackling drug-resistant ERα variants.

papers.title: Virtual Screening and Molecular Dynamics Simulations Identifying Natural Product-Derived Cathepsin K Inhibitors as Potential Therapeutics for Osteoporosis.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis is a prevalent skeletal disorder characterized by excessive bone resorption and an increased risk of fragility fracture. Cathepsin K (CatK), a lysosomal cysteine protease predominantly expressed in osteoclasts, is an established target for anti-resorptive drug development. Here, an integrated computational workflow comprising virtual screening, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, molecular mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, and drug-likeness/ADMET prediction was used to prioritize natural product-derived CatK ligands from th
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline—virtual screening, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM/PBSA binding free energy calculations, and ADMET prediction—to identify natural product-derived compounds that inhibit cathepsin K, a protease central to bone resorption in osteoporosis. The workflow prioritized candidate ligands with favorable binding stability and drug-like properties, nominating them as potential starting points for anti-resorptive therapeutics.

papers.title: Donor-Type-Dependent Heterogeneity of Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Lung Transplantation: A Multi-Cohort Transcriptomic Interaction Analysis of DCD Versus DBD Lungs.
papers.abstract: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) and donation after brain death (DBD) donor lungs are widely used in lung transplantation yet managed as equivalent with respect to ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), despite fundamentally different ischemic backgrounds: warm ischemia in DCD versus neurogenic-inflammatory priming in DBD donors.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-cohort transcriptomic interaction analysis to compare ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) between DCD and DBD donor lungs in transplantation. It finds that IRI responses are heterogeneous and donor-type-dependent, with distinct molecular signatures reflecting warm ischemia in DCD versus neurogenic-inflammatory priming in DBD lungs. The results suggest that DCD and DBD lungs should not be managed as equivalent with respect to IRI.

papers.title: Proteogenomic Profiling of Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Identifies Sex-Differential Proteins and Candidate Therapeutic Targets.
papers.abstract: Current biomarkers for idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) lack disease specificity and provide limited biological insight. We hypothesized that integrating population-based proteomics with genetic evidence would identify robust IPAH-associated proteins relevant to risk stratification, early detection, prognosis, sex differences, and candidate drug-repurposing opportunities.
papers.summary: This study integrates population-based proteomics with genetic evidence to identify proteins associated with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH), revealing sex-differential protein signatures and candidate therapeutic targets. The findings aim to improve risk stratification, early detection, and prognosis for IPAH, while also highlighting potential drug-repurposing opportunities.

papers.title: TRPM8 virtual screening: the essential role of target-specific, inactive-enriched machine-learning scoring functions.
papers.abstract: The Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 8 (TRPM8) ion channel is an emerging therapeutic target implicated in pain, inflammation and other disorders. While structure-based virtual screening (VS) is widely used in drug discovery, the effectiveness of generic and target-specific machine-learning (ML) scoring functions (SFs) for ion channels such as TRPM8 remains to be investigated. We established the first comprehensive structure-based VS benchmark for TRPM8. This evaluates classical docking SFs, generic ML SFs and target-specific ML models retrospectively across multiple TRPM8 protein confo
papers.summary: This study establishes the first comprehensive structure-based virtual screening benchmark for the TRPM8 ion channel, a therapeutic target for pain and inflammation. It compares classical docking scoring functions, generic machine-learning scoring functions, and target-specific ML models, finding that target-specific models trained with inactive-enriched data are essential for effective screening. The work highlights the importance of tailoring ML scoring functions to the specific target rather than relying on generic approaches.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: This paper introduces KAN-GIN, a drug-target affinity prediction framework that swaps the standard multilayer perceptron in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder for a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation, paired with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. Evaluated on DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline, it tests whether this adaptive nonlinear transformation improves affinity prediction.

papers.title: Multi-Endpoint Prediction of Bioactivity and ADMET Properties Coupled with Multi-Objective Optimization in Molecular Descriptor Space for Candidate ERα Antagonists.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Candidate estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) antagonists should combine strong inhibitory activity with favorable absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET)-related properties. This study developed an integrated framework for multi-endpoint prediction, multi-objective optimization in molecular descriptor space, and prioritization of feasible solutions. Methods: A dataset of 1974 compounds with 729 molecular descriptors, pIC50 values, and five binary ADMET-related endpoints was analyzed. Key descriptors were identified through two-stage cross-method and cross-e
papers.summary: This study builds an integrated computational framework that predicts multiple bioactivity and ADMET endpoints for potential ERα antagonists and then optimizes molecular descriptors to prioritize candidates balancing potency and drug-likeness. Using a dataset of 1974 compounds with 729 descriptors, the authors identify key features and apply multi-objective optimization to rank feasible solutions. The work offers a practical pipeline for early-stage drug discovery targeting ERα.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically examines the current state of molecular docking studies applied to natural products, highlighting that methodological quality remains highly variable despite advances in algorithms and AI. It analyzes the specific challenges posed by different natural-product classes and protein targets, and proposes practical guidelines to improve rigor and reproducibility in this widely used structure-based drug discovery approach.

papers.title: Retrieval-Guided Transfer Learning for Low-Resource Ebola Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction plays an important role in computational drug discovery; however, its application to emerging infectious diseases such as Ebola remains challenging because of the limited availability of experimentally measured affinity data. To address this low-resource setting, we propose a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework that leverages BindingDB interactions to improve Ebola DTA prediction. The framework uses a two-stage strategy. In Stage I, source interactions are selected using random sampling, compound-similarity retrieval, protein-similarity retrieval,
papers.summary: This paper presents a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework for predicting drug-target affinity (DTA) in Ebola, a setting with very limited experimental affinity data. It leverages the larger BindingDB interaction dataset and uses compound- and protein-similarity retrieval to select the most relevant source interactions for transfer, aiming to improve prediction accuracy in low-resource infectious disease drug discovery.

papers.title: Confidence-Gated Triage: Coupling Drug-Target Affinity and ADME-T Predictions to Prioritise Compounds for Docking.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Molecular docking and molecular dynamics are accurate but computationally expensive, so the compounds entering them must be chosen well. The present study proposes CADT, a confidence-gated affinity-ADME-T docking-triage cascade that decides which compounds are worth docking. Methods: The gate combines an ensemble estimate of drug-target affinity with its epistemic uncertainty and an applicability-domain check. Predicted absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADME-T) developability is added as a soft flag. All components were trained on openly lice
papers.summary: The authors present CADT, a triage cascade that uses an ensemble drug-target affinity model with uncertainty estimates and an applicability-domain check, plus ADME-T developability predictions, to decide which compounds are worth running through expensive docking and molecular dynamics. The goal is to prioritize compounds more efficiently by gating them on prediction confidence rather than docking everything.

papers.title: Integrated Machine Learning and Molecular Simulation-Guided Discovery of Novel Small-Molecule PD-L1 Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The programmed death-1/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) immune checkpoint is a key therapeutic target in cancer immunotherapy, but small-molecule inhibition remains challenging due to its shallow and dynamic interaction interface. This study aimed to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-guided workflow to identify novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-L1 dimer interface. Methods: A combined computational and experimental approach was established. A support vector regression-genetic algorithm (SVR-GA) model was trained on a dataset of 1385 known PD-L1
papers.summary: This study developed an AI-guided workflow combining support vector regression-genetic algorithm modeling with molecular simulation to discover novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-L1 dimer interface for cancer immunotherapy. The approach identified candidate compounds that were validated experimentally, addressing the challenge of targeting PD-L1's shallow and dynamic interaction interface.

papers.title: Big Data and Artificial Intelligence in Cancer Drug Discovery: Promise, Challenges, and Emerging Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Oncologic drug development is lengthy (~14 years) and expensive (~1.2 billion USD) with low clinical trial success rates (4.1%). Big data and artificial intelligence (AI) are widely proposed as tools to address these challenges. In this review, we examine the current performance and future potential of big data and AI applied to preclinical discovery and development, clinical trials, and the regulatory approval process. We first examine the data foundation required for effective AI, including data harmonization, data commons, and analytical tools. We then assess preclinical applications spanni
papers.summary: This review examines how big data and AI are being applied across the cancer drug development pipeline, from preclinical discovery through clinical trials and regulatory approval. It highlights the data infrastructure requirements (harmonization, data commons, analytical tools) needed for effective AI, while assessing current performance and future opportunities against the backdrop of lengthy, expensive, and low-success-rate oncology drug development.

papers.title: Development of an Interpretable QSAR Model for Predicting Coagulation Factor XIIa Inhibitors Using Ensemble Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Activated coagulation factor XII (FXIIa) is a component of the contact activation pathway and a pharmacologically relevant target in contact-system-associated processes. In this study, scaffold-aware and interpretable machine-learning QSAR models were developed for human FXIIa activity. Methods: Bioactivity records for the human single protein target CHEMBL2821 were retrieved from ChEMBL release 37. Modeling was restricted to exact IC50 measurements from assays explicitly referring to FXIIa, Factor XIIa, or activated Factor XII. Median-consolidated pIC50 values and two-di
papers.summary: This study developed interpretable machine-learning QSAR models to predict inhibitors of coagulation factor XIIa (FXIIa), a target in the contact activation pathway. Using IC50 data from ChEMBL and ensemble methods with scaffold-aware validation, the models aim to support drug discovery for contact-system-associated processes.

papers.title: An AI-Assisted Workflow for Rapid Prioritization of FDA-Approved Drugs as HDAC3 Inhibitor Candidates for Drug Repurposing.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation through histone acetylation plays a critical role in gene expression and cancer progression. Because of its pivotal role in chromatin remodeling, Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) has become a promising therapeutic target. In this study, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven strategy was utilized to prioritize potential HDAC3 inhibitors among FDA-approved compounds to accelerate drug repurposing for cancer therapy. Existing HDAC3 inhibitors were identified in the BindingDB and were used to develop a machine learning (ML) model trained on the most potent inhibitors to identif
papers.summary: This study developed an AI/machine-learning workflow to screen FDA-approved drugs and prioritize candidates likely to inhibit HDAC3, an epigenetic enzyme implicated in cancer. The approach aims to accelerate drug repurposing by identifying existing approved compounds that could be redirected as HDAC3 inhibitors for cancer therapy.

papers.title: An Explainable Machine Learning-Based QSAR Framework for Predicting Thrombin Inhibitory Activity.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Public thrombin bioactivity records contain heterogeneous endpoints, replicate measurements, related chemical series, and potentially reactive compounds that may bias quantitative structure-activity relationship models. In this study, we developed an explainable, assay-aware, and leakage-safe machine learning framework for predicting thrombin-inhibitory activity. Methods: Exact Ki and IC50 records for human thrombin (CHEMBL204) were standardized, converted to pActivity, and aggregated using predefined criteria. The final dataset comprised 5189 unique compounds represente
papers.summary: This study develops an explainable machine learning QSAR framework for predicting thrombin inhibitory activity, addressing common pitfalls like heterogeneous assay endpoints, replicate measurements, and data leakage. Using 5,189 unique compounds from ChEMBL, the authors standardized Ki and IC50 records and applied leakage-safe modeling to produce interpretable predictions. The work offers a more rigorous template for building trustworthy bioactivity prediction models.

papers.title: AI-Powered Marine Drug Discovery: A Putative Dual c-Met/VEGFR2 Lead Candidate for Hepatocellular Carcinoma via Deep Learning and Multiscale Simulation.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality. The c-Met and VEGFR2 pathways synergistically drive HCC progression. Marine natural products offer chemically diverse drug reservoirs; however, conventional activity-guided isolation faces labor intensity, low throughput, and frequent compound rediscovery, limiting marine drug development.
papers.summary: This study uses deep learning combined with multiscale molecular simulations to identify a marine natural product as a putative dual inhibitor of c-Met and VEGFR2 for treating hepatocellular carcinoma. The approach aims to overcome the bottlenecks of traditional activity-guided isolation, such as low throughput and compound rediscovery, by computationally prioritizing marine compounds.

papers.title: Multi-target cell membrane chromatography intelligent screening strategy and its application in drug discovery.
papers.abstract: • MCMC-ISW enables paradigm shift from single-to-multi-target biomimetic screening via CMC and AI-driven recognition and analysis. • Three pathways (mixed membranes, arrays, organoids) enable parallel and physiological multi-target screening. • Whole-genome pan-GPCR library provides target coverage and resource for multi-target screening and receptor-ligand studies. • Platform validates multi-target synergy of TCM formulas and accelerates hit discovery from herbal and compound libraries. • MCMC-ISW offers methodological support and tool references for complex systems and advancing multi-target
papers.summary: This paper introduces MCMC-ISW, a multi-target cell membrane chromatography platform that combines biomimetic screening with AI-driven recognition to move beyond single-target drug screening. It supports three parallel screening pathways (mixed membranes, arrays, and organoids) and includes a whole-genome pan-GPCR library for receptor-ligand studies. The platform was applied to validate multi-target synergy of traditional Chinese medicine formulas and to accelerate hit discovery from herbal and compound libraries.

papers.title: AlloPool is a deep learning framework that infers protein allostery from molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have transformed protein structure prediction and design. However, protein function is governed not only by static structures but also by the conformational dynamics that allow proteins to access distinct functional states. Predicting these dynamic transitions, central to many biological processes, remains challenging due to the scarcity of high-resolution experimental data, which limits the training of machine-learning models for dynamic and energetic property prediction. Here, we present AlloPool, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that in
papers.summary: AlloPool is a graph neural network framework that predicts protein allostery—how binding at one site affects function at a distant site—by learning from molecular dynamics simulations. It addresses the scarcity of experimental data on protein conformational dynamics by leveraging simulation-derived data to train models that capture dynamic and energetic properties. This offers a new computational route to infer allosteric mechanisms without relying solely on static structures.

papers.title: Skin Aging: From Molecular Mechanisms to Therapeutic and Technological Innovations.
papers.abstract: Aging is a complex, pervasive biological process that causes irreversible declines in function across organ systems. The skin, the body's largest organ, interfaces directly with the external environment and undergoes aging driven by intrinsic (chronological) and extrinsic (environmental) factors, which result in functional deterioration and greater susceptibility to related disorders. Although numerous anti-aging strategies have been investigated, relatively few specifically target the skin. This review delineates the principal phenotypes and underlying mechanisms of skin aging. Phenotypic hal
papers.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on skin aging, covering both intrinsic (chronological) and extrinsic (environmental) drivers and their resulting phenotypes. It also surveys emerging therapeutic and technological strategies specifically aimed at countering skin aging. The paper serves as a broad overview rather than presenting new experimental data.

papers.title: Extraction, Phytochemical Profiling, and Computational Evaluation of Corymbia citriodora Essential Oil as a COX-2 Inhibitor: Steam vs. Microwave-Assisted Distillation, GC-MS/MS, Docking, DFT, and MD Simulations.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic inflammation sustained by cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) underlies many human diseases, while the cardiovascular liabilities of coxibs have renewed interest in plant-derived alternatives. This study characterised the volatile composition of Corymbia citriodora essential oil under two distillation regimes and identified constituents able to inhibit human COX-2 and iNOS. Methods: Oils obtained by steam distillation (SD) and microwave-assisted steam distillation (MSD) were profiled by GC-MS/MS. All identified constituents were sc
papers.summary: This study compared steam distillation and microwave-assisted steam distillation for extracting Corymbia citriodora essential oil, profiling the volatile compounds by GC-MS/MS. Computational docking, DFT, and molecular dynamics simulations were then used to identify oil constituents that could inhibit COX-2 and iNOS, suggesting plant-derived alternatives to coxibs for inflammation.

papers.title: Phytochemical Analysis Using LC-MS/MS and Anticancer Activity of Asphodelus tenuifolius Roots: Cell Cycle Arrest, Apoptosis, and In Silico Insights.
papers.abstract: Asphodelus tenuifolius Cav. (Asphodelaceae) is traditionally used in North African ethnomedicine for inflammatory and oxidative stress-related disorders. In this study, the hydroethanolic root extract was investigated by LC-HRMS/MS, leading to the identification of 58 metabolites, mainly flavonoids, anthraquinones, and cinnamic acid derivatives. Major constituents included luteolin, emodin, luteolin-7-O-β-D-glucoside, subaphyllin (N-trans-feruloylputrescine), and N-trans-feruloyltyramine. The extract showed moderate antiproliferative activity against MDA-MB-231 and PC-3 cells, while flow cytom
papers.summary: This study used LC-MS/MS to identify 58 metabolites, mainly flavonoids, anthraquinones, and cinnamic acid derivatives, from the hydroethanolic root extract of Asphodelus tenuifolius. The extract showed moderate anticancer activity against MDA-MB-231 and PC-3 cell lines, inducing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, with in silico docking suggesting potential molecular targets.

papers.title: Exploring the Multitarget Pharmacological Potential of Halogeton sativus Secondary Metabolites: An Integrated Experimental and Computational Approach.
papers.abstract: This study offers an in-depth analysis of Halogeton sativus, traditionally consumed in the Mediterranean region. Phytochemical investigation of crude extracts allowed the isolation and spectroscopic identification of 15 secondary metabolites. α-Amylase inhibitory and anti-inflammatory activities were determined via the caraway iodine method, heat-induced lysis, and denaturation inhibition assays, respectively. The antimicrobial activity was tested using a disc diffusion method, and the antioxidant effects were assessed by six methods. The ethyl acetate extract (HS-EtOAc) showed a stronger α-am
papers.summary: This study isolated 15 secondary metabolites from the Mediterranean plant Halogeton sativus and tested their extracts for α-amylase inhibition, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant activities. The ethyl acetate extract showed the strongest α-amylase inhibition, and computational analyses were integrated to explore multitarget pharmacological potential.

papers.title: In Vitro Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Sour Cherry (Prunus cerasus L.) Seed Oil and Computational Safety Profiling.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the in vitro anti-inflammatory activity of sour cherry seed oils, including samples obtained by Soxhlet extraction and maceration, as well as ten commercial samples. The results demonstrated that the 15-lipoxygenase inhibitory activity of the oil samples ranged from 6% to 80%. Regarding cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibition, while most samples showed negligible activity, the oil produced by Soxhlet extraction inhibited COX-1 and COX-2 by 38% and 32%, respectively. Similarly, the oil obtained via maceration showed inhibition rates of 25% and 23% for COX-1 and COX-2, respe
papers.summary: This study evaluated the anti-inflammatory properties of sour cherry seed oils from different extraction methods and commercial sources, finding that 15-lipoxygenase inhibition ranged widely from 6% to 80%. Soxhlet-extracted oil showed the strongest COX-1 and COX-2 inhibition (38% and 32%), while most commercial samples had negligible COX activity. Computational safety profiling was also performed to assess the oils' suitability.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, Antimycobacterial Evaluation, and In Silico Investigation of Benzisothiazole-Based Hydrazide Derivatives as Potential Anti-Tuberculosis Agents.
papers.abstract: A series of novel benzisothiazole-based hydrazide derivatives was rationally designed, synthesized, and evaluated for their antitubercular activity. Among the synthesized compounds, derivative 8k emerged as the most potent candidate, exhibiting a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 0.25 μg/mL, along with a high selectivity index (SI) of 42 and confirmed bactericidal activity. To gain preliminary insights into its possible mechanism of action, compound 8k was subjected to molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, using enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (InhA) as the
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized a series of benzisothiazole-based hydrazide derivatives and tested them against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The most potent compound, 8k, showed strong antitubercular activity (MIC 0.25 μg/mL) with good selectivity and bactericidal effects, and docking plus molecular dynamics simulations suggested it may act by inhibiting the InhA enzyme.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven decoding of maternal immune signatures in repeated pregnancy loss.
papers.abstract: Repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) is a multifactorial condition in which the underlying immunological mechanisms, particularly the disruption of maternal-fetal tolerance, remain incompletely understood. Although immune tolerance is critical for pregnancy success, the specific immune dysregulations contributing to RPL, particularly in euploid pregnancies, have been difficult to characterize. To address this, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissues from RPL patients and first-trimester controls. Our analysis initially revealed elevated expression of a transcriptional module of im
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissue from patients with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and first-trimester controls, combined with machine learning, to identify maternal immune signatures associated with the condition. The analysis reveals elevated expression of a specific transcriptional module in immune cells, highlighting disrupted maternal-fetal tolerance mechanisms in euploid pregnancies.

papers.title: Repurposing antifungal drugs for Oral squamous cell carcinoma using network pharmacology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics approaches.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains an important cause of cancer morbidity and mortality, and new multi-target approaches are required to increase therapeutic options. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to identify new anticancer applications for clinically approved drugs with established safety profiles. An integrative in silico workflow was designed to identify overlapping targets between selected antifungal drugs and OSCC-associated genes based on network pharmacology and protein-protein interaction analysis. Network pharmacology identified 144 common targets for antifunga
papers.summary: This study uses an in silico workflow combining network pharmacology, protein-protein interaction analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics to identify shared targets between approved antifungal drugs and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). The authors found 144 common targets, suggesting antifungal agents could be repurposed as multi-target OSCC therapeutics. The work is computational only and lacks experimental validation.

papers.title: Cannabis as a source of novel therapeutics: A computational study combining LBDD and structure-based docking/dynamics to identify novel drug-like compounds for colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Cannabis represents a valuable source of bioactive compounds with significant therapeutic potential, thanks to its rich phytochemical profile, making it a prime candidate for cancer research. Our study investigates the potential of cannabis-derived compounds to inhibit cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2), a crucial regulator of cell-cycle progression and colorectal cancer cell proliferation. A comprehensive computational workflow integrating 3D-QSAR modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, drug-likeness assessment, and ADMET prediction was employed to investigate a dataset of
papers.summary: This computational study screened cannabis-derived phytochemicals for their ability to inhibit CDK2, a key cell-cycle regulator implicated in colorectal cancer proliferation. Using 3D-QSAR modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET/drug-likeness predictions, the authors identified candidate compounds with favorable binding and pharmacokinetic profiles. The work proposes cannabis as a source of novel drug-like CDK2 inhibitors warranting further experimental validation.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Computational screening of Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as potential aromatase inhibitors: Molecular docking, ADMET, Network pharmacology, Molecular dynamics simulation, and DFT studies" [Pharmaceutic. Sci. Adv. 4 (2026) 100108].
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.pscia.2026.100108.].
papers.summary: This is a corrigendum notice correcting the original article on computational screening of Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as aromatase inhibitors. It contains no new scientific findings, only corrections to the previously published work.

papers.title: Computational evaluation of EPA-PC binding to GCase in neuronopathic Gaucher disease.
papers.abstract: Gaucher disease (GD) is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient acid β-glucosidase (GCase) activity and consequent accumulation of glucosylceramide. Current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies improve several systemic manifestations but have limited impact on neuronopathic disease, motivating evaluation of alternative molecular strategies. This study computationally assessed the interaction of EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, with human GCase (PDB ID: 2NSX). The protein structure was examined by Ramachandran analysis and hydroph
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and structural analysis to evaluate whether EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, can bind to the lysosomal enzyme GCase, which is deficient in neuronopathic Gaucher disease. The work suggests a potential molecular interaction that could inform alternative therapeutic strategies for forms of the disease that respond poorly to current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies.

papers.title: Computational Repurposing of Janus Kinase Inhibitors as Potential Therapeutic Candidates for Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common neurodegenerative disorder, and current therapies provide only limited symptomatic relief without effectively slowing its progression. Increasing evidence suggests that aberrant activation of the Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT) signaling cascade contributes to AD-associated neuroinflammation. This study investigated the therapeutic potential and molecular mechanisms of JAK inhibitors in AD using integrated bioinformatics and network pharmacology approaches. Materials and Methods: Pot
papers.summary: This study uses integrated bioinformatics and network pharmacology to explore whether Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors could be repurposed as treatments for Alzheimer's disease, based on the role of JAK/STAT signaling in AD-related neuroinflammation. The authors identify potential JAK inhibitor candidates and propose molecular mechanisms linking JAK/STAT inhibition to AD pathology, though the abstract is truncated before results are fully described.

papers.title: FOXC1 drives lung cancer metastasis and functions as a target for AI-enabled anti-metastatic drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer metastasis remains the leading cause of treatment failure and death. Forkhead box C1 (FOXC1) promotes cancer progression, but its definitive mechanism in lung cancer metastasis and druggable potential remain unclear. This study aimed to clarify the mechanism and develop a FOXC1-targeted inhibitor.
papers.summary: This study identifies FOXC1 as a key driver of lung cancer metastasis and demonstrates that it can be targeted therapeutically. The authors use AI-enabled drug discovery to develop a FOXC1-targeted inhibitor, providing a potential new strategy for treating metastatic lung cancer.

papers.title: Transforming Nanomaterials Development with Artificial Intelligence Techniques.
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into various scientific fields is reshaping traditional methodologies, and nanotechnology is no exception. This article explores the transformative impact of AI on nanotechnology, a domain focused on manipulating matter at atomic and molecular scales to develop novel materials with tailored properties. Historically, the discovery and optimization of nanomaterials relied on labor-intensive trial-and-error methods, often taking years to yield practical results. We examine how recent advances in AI particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning,
papers.summary: This review article examines how artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, is transforming nanotechnology by accelerating the discovery and optimization of nanomaterials. It argues that AI can replace traditional labor-intensive trial-and-error approaches, enabling faster development of materials with tailored properties.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven drug discovery: a deep learning paradigm shift in pharmaceutical research and development.
papers.abstract: Efficient drug discovery is essential to mitigate the high attrition rates and capital-intensive nature of traditional pharmaceutical research. Deep learning (DL) has catalyzed a paradigm shift, offering unprecedented computational capabilities to accelerate this process. This review systematically summarizes advancements in DL methodologies for drug discovery. First, the critical data foundations, Molecular Representation Learning, and core architectures underpinning artificial intelligence (AI)-driven therapeutics are elucidated, with a particular emphasis on the evolution of generative AI f
papers.summary: This review surveys how deep learning is reshaping drug discovery, covering data foundations, molecular representation learning, and core neural architectures. It emphasizes the rise of generative AI for designing novel therapeutic candidates and aims to map the current methodological landscape.

papers.title: Network biology to artificial intelligence: building the next generation of predictive drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Drug discovery remains constrained by high attrition rates, prolonged timelines, and limited ability to translate molecular insights into effective therapies. Although reductionist approaches targeting individual molecules have delivered transformative medicines, successful patient-centric treatment remains a major challenge. Furthermore, increasing evidence demonstrates that therapeutic outcomes emerge from complex, dynamic, and context-dependent biological networks. Systems biology has provided a framework to understand these interactions, yet its predictive capability has been limited by bi
papers.summary: This review argues that drug discovery's high failure rates stem from reductionist single-target approaches and that therapeutic outcomes emerge from complex biological networks. It proposes integrating systems biology with artificial intelligence to build next-generation predictive drug discovery frameworks that better capture context-dependent network effects.

papers.title: RA-PLA: Retrieval-augmented graph convolutional networks for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand binding affinity (PLA) prediction is essential for computational drug discovery, yet existing deep learning methods typically employ a single globally trained model that fails to adapt to individual query samples. In this paper, we propose a novel end-to-end framework that retrieves hard protein-ligand pairs-samples whose nearest neighbors have conflicting labels under manifold smoothness constraints-and integrates them via a semi-supervised graph convolutional network (GCN). For each query, we automatically construct a graph where nodes represent protein-ligand pairs and edges
papers.summary: The authors introduce RA-PLA, a framework that improves protein-ligand binding affinity prediction by retrieving 'hard' training examples—pairs whose nearest neighbors have conflicting labels—and incorporating them through a semi-supervised graph convolutional network. This retrieval-augmented approach adapts predictions to individual query samples rather than relying on a single globally trained model, aiming to boost accuracy in computational drug discovery.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in non-small cell lung cancer: transforming diagnosis, treatment, and prognostic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is characterized by profound biological heterogeneity, frequently leading to late-stage diagnosis, recurrence, or metastasis. Conventional clinical pathways heavily depend on subjective visual interpretations, invasive tissue biopsies, and experience-based medical models that constrain individualized precision medicine. Identifying noninvasive, cross-scale tools for whole-disease-course assessment is critical for optimizing clinical decision-making and survival outcomes. This review critically synthesizes recent research progress and core algorithmic applicat
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in applying artificial intelligence to non-small cell lung cancer across diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis. It highlights how AI can address limitations of conventional clinical pathways, which rely on subjective interpretation and invasive biopsies, by enabling noninvasive, cross-scale assessment for precision medicine. The paper surveys core algorithmic applications and their potential to improve clinical decision-making and survival outcomes.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in experimental and clinical in vitro analysis: applications, limitations, and future directions.
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into in vitro analyses represents a transformative shift in laboratory medicine, diagnostics, and pharmaceutical research. Traditional in vitro methods, from cell culture assays to high-throughput screening, rely on manual interpretation and conventional statistics. Machine and deep learning now automate image analysis, improve diagnostic accuracy, accelerate drug discovery, and enhance quality control. Convolutional neural networks and predictive models have reported specialist-level performance in cell segmentation, biomarker detection, and patholog
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning and deep learning are being integrated into in vitro laboratory workflows, including cell culture assays, high-throughput screening, and diagnostic pathology. It highlights reported specialist-level performance of convolutional neural networks in tasks like cell segmentation and biomarker detection, while also discussing current limitations and future directions for AI in experimental and clinical in vitro analysis.

papers.title: Designing novel linagliptin analogs through combined generative artificial intelligence, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and binding energy estimation for targeting fibroblast activation protein.
papers.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is a highly specific biomarker overexpressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts, making it a promising diagnostic target. Developing novel high-affinity molecular probes for FAP-targeted diagnostics remains an active area of research. In this study, an integrated computational pipeline combining generative artificial intelligence, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, binding energy estimation, and pharmacokinetic predictions was used to design and evaluate novel linagliptin-based compounds as potential FAP-binding analogs. From a preliminary
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline combining generative AI, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and binding energy calculations to design novel linagliptin-based compounds targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a biomarker overexpressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts. The work identifies candidate analogs with predicted high binding affinity and favorable pharmacokinetic properties, offering potential leads for FAP-targeted cancer diagnostics.

papers.title: Therapeutic Antitoxoplasmosis Potential of Garcinia cambogia: Evidence From In Silico and In Vivo Studies.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii, an opportunistic protozoan, is widely prevalent and poses potential health risks. Its treatment remains challenging with several side effects, urging the exploration of new, safe, and efficient drugs. We aimed to explore the therapeutic efficacy of the medicinal plant Garcinia cambogia (GC) against both acute and chronic toxoplasmosis. Sixty Swiss albino mice were allocated into five groups: I (healthy), II (model), III (spiramycin [SPM] treated, IV (GC treated), and V (SPM + GC treated). Each group is further divided into two subgroups receiving treatment at 4 and 42 days p
papers.summary: This study evaluated Garcinia cambogia (GC) extract as a treatment for acute and chronic Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice, combining computational (in silico) predictions with in vivo experiments. GC treatment, alone and in combination with the standard drug spiramycin, was tested across five mouse groups, with outcomes assessed at early and late infection timepoints. The findings suggest GC has therapeutic potential against toxoplasmosis, though the abstract is truncated and specific efficacy results are not fully detailed.

papers.title: Design and syntheses of 4-aminoquinoline-thiazolidinone hybrids as anti-protozoal agents.
papers.abstract: Molecular hybridization is an effective approach employed to synthesize molecules that possess the ability to function as dual inhibitors, thereby addressing the issue of growing resistance. Resistance by the malaria parasite is one such example. Therefore, the study aims to develop hybrid compounds consisting of 4-aminoquinoline and 4-thiazolidinone, utilizing molecular docking for sorting, followed by synthesis and evaluation of their anti-malarial potential.
papers.summary: This study designed hybrid molecules combining 4-aminoquinoline and 4-thiazolidinone scaffolds as potential dual-action anti-protozoal agents to combat drug resistance in malaria. Molecular docking was used to prioritize candidates, which were then synthesized and evaluated for anti-malarial activity. The work represents an early-stage medicinal chemistry effort toward new hybrid antimalarials.

papers.title: Drug Repurposing for Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease: Current Evidence, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is a prevalent chronic liver condition with limited approved pharmacotherapies. Drug repurposing offers a time-efficient alternative to de novo development, yet existing reviews often compile candidate compounds without critically appraising the methodological robustness, evidence quality, or translational barriers. In this review, we evaluated current repurposing strategies, including real-world data analyses, computational screening, and experimental validations. As a preliminary search for this review, we searched PubMed and clini
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates drug repurposing strategies for metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), a common chronic liver condition with few approved treatments. It examines real-world data analyses, computational screening, and experimental validation approaches, while assessing the methodological rigor, evidence quality, and translational barriers that existing reviews often overlook.

papers.title: Cross-fusion of digital twins and artificial intelligence in diabetes: from mechanistic elucidation to full-cycle precision management.
papers.abstract: The integration of digital twins (DT) and artificial intelligence (AI) is driving a paradigm shift in diabetes mellitus (DM) care from traditional population-based, symptomatic intervention to a lifecycle-oriented precision management approach. This review systematically elaborates on the cross-disciplinary integration mechanisms of the two technologies. By integrating multimodal data and constructing physiologically constrained hybrid models, it achieves multi-scale mechanistic analyses ranging from single-cell β-cell protection to multi-organ complications at the basic research level. On the
papers.summary: This review describes how combining digital twins with artificial intelligence can transform diabetes care from population-level symptom treatment to personalized, lifecycle-oriented precision management. It highlights the use of multimodal data and physiologically constrained hybrid models to analyze mechanisms from single-cell beta-cell protection to multi-organ complications.

papers.title: Structure-based molecular modeling of a novel S-Remiketamine scaffold and derived arylcyclohexanone analogues: NMDA receptor dynamics, MM-GBSA ranking, and CES1-Oriented structural compatibility.
papers.abstract: Short-acting ketamine-related scaffold design remains an important medicinal-chemistry problem, but computational studies require conservative interpretation until receptor, enzymatic, and pharmacokinetic validation is available.
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based molecular modeling to design a novel S-Remiketamine scaffold and related arylcyclohexanone analogues, evaluating their interactions with the NMDA receptor via dynamics simulations and MM-GBSA binding ranking. It also assesses structural compatibility with CES1, the enzyme involved in ketamine metabolism, to explore short-acting ketamine-like compounds. The authors emphasize that these computational predictions require experimental validation of receptor binding, enzymatic processing, and pharmacokinetics.
